title: Single-loop bullion
subtitle: A compact bullion knot variant for tiny curved petals and stamens
excerpt: A single-loop bullion wraps the thread around the needle just enough times to form a tight, curved barrel that lies flat without the bulk of a full bullion knot.
sourceNotes: Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), knot stitch variations.

glossaryTerms.definition: The tight coil of wrapped thread that forms the body of a bullion knot. The number of wraps determines the length and curve of the barrel.

heroPrompt: Several single-loop bullion knots forming tiny curved flower stamens on white cotton, close-up, natural light.

content.text: A single-loop bullion forms a short, tight

by wrapping the thread around the needle only 4 to 6 times instead of the 8 to 12 wraps of a standard bullion knot. The result is a small curved stitch suited to stamens, flower centres, and tiny leaf details.

items.label: Needle
items.value: Embroidery needle size 9 (must have a consistent width along the shaft)

content.text: Bring the needle up at point A. Insert it back down at point B, about 4 mm away, but do not pull through. The needle tip exits at A.
Wrap the thread around the needle 4 to 6 times, close to the fabric surface.
Hold the wraps down with your thumb and pull the needle through carefully. The wraps form the barrel.
Insert the needle back at B to anchor the barrel. It will curve slightly if the wraps slightly exceed the distance between A and B.

items.symptom: The barrel slides off as you pull through
items.cause: Not enough tension held on the wraps.
items.fix: Press the wraps firmly against the fabric with your thumb as you pull the needle through.

items.symptom: The stitch lies flat rather than curving
items.cause: The number of wraps matches the distance AB exactly.
items.fix: Add one or two more wraps so the barrel is slightly longer than the gap.

content.text: Single-loop bullions cluster together to form flower stamens, rosebuds, and compact seed heads. They are the starting point for Brazilian embroidery, which uses longer bullions wrapped many times to form petals.
